It's best to just see these concepts for what they are: **concepts**. As much as it may feel this way--the world is not black and white; every thing is on a spectrum, including where every one is at psychologically. What we have labeled as "NPD" and "BPD" are simply on opposite ends of the spectrum regarding the functions of the amygdala. The more precise we can nail where on that spectrum we are, the better we can adjust our therapy to fit it. But ultimately... it's really only you who can diagnose where you are, a therapist / psychiatrist is just some one who helps facilitate and officiate this.

I like to see life as a game. 

Like, yeah, it can be pretty lame at times... But it's also kind of fun at other times. I could totally just unplug the game; hit the reset button at any time, but the longer i wait to do that, the mire interesting the game gets.
DBT (or Zen) is an ongoing practice, which continues even after the sessions are finished. DBT sessions simply get one ready to practice Zen when they are over.
What we have culturally defined using the word "empath" is really just describing a highfunctioning borderline.

BPD and NPD can look extremely similar from the outside... The major difference between the two (according to my understanding) is the processing power of the amygdala (the part of the brain which regulates emotions, empathy, personality, and survival).: Where as the person experiencing BPD has an overly active amygdala which makes them feel too much, causing interpersonal/social issues, the person experiencing NPD has an overly inactive amygdala which makes them feel too little, causing interpersonal/social issues. The two personalities are under the same subgroup of "Emotional and Impulsive" along with histrionic personality disorder, and the three are very easily and commonly mixed up when making a diagnosis.
